text:
A world like a severed tree.

A rooted-out generation.

Men with no destiny but
to shore up the ruins.


To break the sea
in the sea, like an immense hymen,
the trees rock the green silence,
the stars crackle; I hear them.


Only man is alone. It is that he knows himself
alive and mortal. It is that he feels himself fleeing
—that river of time toward death—.


It is that he wants to remain. To keep on going,
to climb, against death, toward the eternal.
He is afraid to look. He closes his eyes
to sleep the sleep of the living.


But death, from within, sees.
But death, from within, keeps watch.
But death, from within, kills.


…The sea—the sea—, like an immense hymen,
the trees moving the green air,
the snow in flames of the light held aloft…

translation.title: The Earth
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish rendering. The repeated anaphora, parenthetical river of time, feminine and masculine sea, and closing images are preserved.
